summaryText:
Pastor Travis Hearn opened the new five-week series, Build My Church, with a challenge: every one of us is building something, so what are we building, and what are we building it on? Drawing on Jesus' words in Matthew 16:18, he reminded the church that Jesus Himself is building His church, and that the gates of hell will not prevail against it. Pastor Travis noted that people build businesses, careers, families, marriages and reputations, but that a life can be successful and still miss what is significant for eternity. Using Jesus' picture of the wise and foolish builders in Matthew 7, he warned against building on approval, comparison, pride, money or status, since storms do not just break foundations, they expose them. He invited everyone to make Jesus their foundation.

The heart of the message came from Nehemiah, who carried a burden for Jerusalem's broken walls and gathered the people with the words, "Come, let us rebuild." Pastor Travis highlighted the word "us" and the repeated phrase "next to him" in Nehemiah 3, showing that God's work is done together, with each person building their own part of the wall. He used the image of picking up your hammer and put it against the temptation to sit in a lawn chair as a spectator or consumer. He encouraged the church to move from watching to participating.

He shared three points. First, everybody has a wall: the church is the shared work we build together, and each person has a part, such as serving, praying, inviting, mentoring, giving or helping with kids. Second, everybody has a hammer: whatever is in your hand, whether gifts, time, talents, treasure, testimony or home, God can use it, and the enemy lies when he says you have nothing to offer. Third, everybody has to build: spiritual maturity moves from asking what the church can do for me to asking what God can do through me in this church. He also encouraged believers to find a church home, plug in and contribute, and to worship with their whole hearts, not only their hands.

Pastor Travis closed by pointing to Nehemiah's wall, completed in 52 days by people working side by side, and challenged everyone to pick up their hammer over the next five weeks. He invited those who had never given their life to Jesus, or who wanted to return to Him, to say yes that day, and he led the church in a prayer of surrender and a desire to build something of eternal significance. Online campus members were reminded that their prayers, generosity and invitations matter, and that they are part of what God is building.
mainPoints: Everybody has a wall: the church is the shared work we build together, and each person is called to build their own part next to others.
Everybody has a hammer: whatever is in your hand, such as your gifts, time, talents, treasure or testimony, can be offered to God for His use.
Everybody has to build: God calls us to move from being spectators and consumers to being builders who serve, give, pray, invite and disciple, on the foundation of Jesus.

versesMentioned.text: And I tell you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church, and the gates of Hades will not overcome it.

Therefore everyone who hears these words of mine and puts them into practice is like a wise man who built his house on the rock. The rain came down, the streams rose, and the winds blew and beat against that house; yet it did not fall, because it had its foundation on the rock. But everyone who hears these words of mine and does not put them into practice is like a foolish man who built his house on sand. The rain came down, the streams rose, and the winds blew and beat against that house, and it fell with a great crash.

Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ loved the church and gave himself up for her to make her holy, cleansing her by the washing with water through the word, and to present her to himself as a radiant church, without stain or wrinkle or any other blemish, but holy and blameless.

Then I said to them, 'You see the trouble we are in: Jerusalem lies in ruins, and its gates have been burned with fire. Come, let us rebuild the wall of Jerusalem, and we will no longer be in disgrace.'
I also told them about the gracious hand of my God on me and what the king had said to me. They replied, 'Let us start rebuilding.' So they began this good work.
The men of Jericho built the adjoining section, and Zaccur son of Imri built next to them.
Therefore, I urge you, brothers and sisters, in view of God's mercy, to offer your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and pleasing to God, this is your true and proper worship.
So the wall was completed on the twenty-fifth of Elul, in fifty-two days.
For he says, 'In the time of my favor I heard you, and in the day of salvation I helped you.' I tell you, now is the time of God's favor, now is the day of salvation.

Monday.scripture: Matthew 7:24 (NIV): "Therefore everyone who hears these words of mine and puts them into practice is like a wise man who built his house on the rock."
Monday.focus: Check your foundation: what are you building your life on?
Monday.action: Take ten quiet minutes to write down what you are currently building (family, work, dreams, reputation). Next to each, note whether it rests on Jesus or on approval, comparison, or status.
Monday.prayer: Jesus, be the foundation of everything I build. Show me any place where I have been building on sand, and help me put your words into practice. Amen.

Tuesday.scripture: Nehemiah 2:18 (NIV): "They replied, 'Let us start rebuilding.' So they began this good work."
Tuesday.focus: Say yes to God: pick up your hammer.
Tuesday.action: Ask God, 'What part are you asking me to play in building your church?' Write down any thoughts that come, then choose one small step you can take this week.
Tuesday.prayer: Lord, here I am. Use my hands, my heart, and my life to help build your church. Show me my part of the wall. Amen.

Wednesday.scripture: 1 Peter 4:10 (NIV): "Each of you should use whatever gift you have received to serve others, as faithful stewards of God's grace in its various forms."
Wednesday.focus: Identify your hammer: the gifts, time, and talents God has placed in your hand.
Wednesday.action: List three things you have to offer (a skill, some time, a testimony, your home). Then sign up for, or reach out about, one way to serve at your church or online campus.
Wednesday.prayer: Father, thank you for the gifts you have given me. Help me steward them faithfully and serve others with joy. Amen.

Thursday.scripture: Hebrews 10:24 (NIV): "And let us consider how we may spur one another on toward love and good deeds."
Thursday.focus: Build next to others: invite and encourage.
Thursday.action: Send a friend, neighbor, or family member an invitation to watch next Sunday's service with you, or send an encouraging message to someone in your church community.
Thursday.prayer: God, give me boldness and kindness to invite others. Prepare hearts to hear your good news, and let me build alongside your people. Amen.

Friday.scripture: 2 Corinthians 9:7 (NIV): "Each of you should give what you have decided in your heart to give, not reluctantly or under compulsion, for God loves a cheerful giver."
Friday.focus: Give generously to the work God is doing through the church.
Friday.action: Prayerfully decide on a gift of money, time, or help that you can offer this week, and follow through with a joyful heart.
Friday.prayer: Lord, everything I have comes from you. Make me a cheerful and generous giver who helps build what will last for eternity. Amen.

Saturday.scripture: Psalm 127:1 (NIV): "Unless the Lord builds the house, the builders labor in vain."
Saturday.focus: Pray for your church and prepare your heart to be a builder, not a spectator.
Saturday.action: Spend time praying for your pastors, your church family, and your online and in-person campuses by name. Then decide on one way you will participate in worship and service this Sunday.
Saturday.prayer: Lord, unless you build your church, our work is in vain. Build your church through me, and keep me from being a spectator. Thank you that your church will stand. Amen.

title: How to Find Your Purpose in God’s Church | Pick Up Your Hammer
